newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Friday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 1.05 billion yuan from 625 million yuan with the one-day contract the most actively traded.
Trading was slightly more active than on Thursday with securities brokerages borrowing money to cover shortages in their accounts due to a new domestic A share issue in Shanghai.
The brokerages can only trade one-day contracts in accordance with exchange rules and this resulted in the one-day contract being the most actively traded, they said.
"Borrowing by the securities brokers was the major factor on Friday," a trader said. "This caused trading in the one-day contract to account for half of the trading volume today."

However, trading remained dull as a whole with the market suffering from an oversupply of funds after the recent crackdown on the stock markets left non-banking financial institutions more cautious about borrowing, traders said.
"Slow activity on the market is likely to cause interbank rates to move in a narrow range in the short term," a second trader said.
